raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# [Perf] paged-experts: fuse slot lookup into decide

## Motivation

This PR aims to increase decode tok/s.

Currently, Paged Experts (#42557) runs 21 graph nodes per paged MoE layer in captured decode. 11 of them are small torch ops that turn the decide kernel's result into the runner's inputs: index the slot of each routed entry, mask padding, mask its weight. On Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 at batch size 1 they take 0.44 ms per step, about 9% of decode.

The decide kernel already knows each routed expert's slot when its eviction loop ends. This PR has it write the runner's inputs directly: the slot and router weight of each routed entry, with slot 0 and weight 0 for padding. The layer's paged part of the graph is then decide plus gather, **10 nodes instead of 21**, and the runner reads its inputs straight from the decide kernel's output.

## Modifications

`paged_experts.cuh`, `paged_experts.py`, `executor.py`:
- After its eviction loop, the decide kernel also writes each routed entry's slot and router weight. Padding entries, and ids outside `[0, E)`, get slot 0 and weight 0.
- The device executor passes these straight to the base method. A paged layer's part of the captured step is now decide plus gather: 10 nodes instead of 21.
- Router weights are passed to the kernel as float32. If they come in another dtype, they are converted back, which is exact.
- `paged_experts_decide` gains `topk_weights`, `run_ids` and `run_w`; it has no other callers. The host-planned (eager) path is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

**Kernel test.** Over 200 random routing steps with padding, the decide kernel's runner inputs equal the reference: each entry's slot from the LRU reference, and its weight, with 0 for padding. Ids outside `[0, E)` count as padding.

**Paged vs unpaged, 4-layer test models** (E=32, top-4, K=8; prompt and greedy decode logprobs; RTX 5070 Ti; main 2d3de82633 and this PR in one run):

| model | runner | this PR | main |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-MoE bf16 | triton | identical | identical |
| AWQ int4 | Marlin | decode max 0.014 | decode max 0.014 |
| compressed-tensors NVFP4 | Marlin | median max 0.076, unpaged floor 0.055 | median max 0.059, unpaged floor 0.063 |

Marlin is not run-to-run reproducible, so the Marlin formats are judged against the spread of two unpaged servers (the floor); bf16 on triton is bit-identical. Each check has a negative control that must fail (a perturbed RMSNorm eps on bf16 and AWQ, unnormalized top-k weights on NVFP4), and all three do.

**GSM8K (200 questions), Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4, K=92:** main 0.950 / 0.935, this PR 0.945.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same machine as #42557: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (PCIe 5.0 x16, 62 GB RAM), Qwen3-30B-A3B, 10,240 KV tokens and 4 slots, prefix caching off, 16 ShareGPT warm-up requests discarded. Decode tok/s is `1000 / median TPOT` over 8 ShareGPT prompts sent one at a time (256 output tokens each); TTFT and ITL are from the same requests. 4 requests: 16 ShareGPT prompts from 4 clients at once (output tok/s). 2k TTFT: 4 natural ~2,048-token prompts. main (upstream 2d3de82633) is measured first and last in the same run as this PR; both values are shown, and a difference inside their spread is no difference.

| config | decode tok/s | TTFT p50 / p99 | ITL p50 / p99 | 4 requests: out tok/s | 2k TTFT p50 | peak VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| int4, K=92: main | 211.8 / 212.8 | 51 / 88, 50 / 82 ms | 4.70 / 5.35, 4.70 / 5.30 ms | 400 / 401 | 247 / 239 ms | 14.7 GiB |
| int4, K=92: this PR | **234.1** (+10.3%) | 50 / 82 ms | **4.27 / 4.90 ms** | **418** (+4.2%) | 248 ms | 14.7 GiB |
| FP8, K=40: main | 90.3 / 90.3 | 213 / 301, 218 / 301 ms | 10.51 / 20.74, 10.51 / 20.76 ms | 100 / 99 | 427 / 424 ms | 13.4 GiB |
| FP8, K=40: this PR | **94.2** (+4.3%) | 219 / 300 ms | **10.04 / 20.26 ms** | 101 | 425 ms | 13.4 GiB |
| NVFP4 (Marlin), K=85: main | 189.8 / 192.9 | 72 / 119, 73 / 116 ms | 5.20 / 6.44, 5.11 / 6.32 ms | 352 / 349 | 248 / 244 ms | 14.5 GiB |
| NVFP4 (Marlin), K=85: this PR | **208.0** (+8.7%) | 76 / 117 ms | **4.76 / 6.12 ms** | **370** (+5.5%) | 248 ms | 14.5 GiB |

Percentages against the mean of the two main runs. The saving is a fixed ~0.42–0.46 ms per captured step (int4 4.71 → 4.27 ms, FP8 11.08 → 10.62 ms, NVFP4 5.23 → 4.81 ms), so it shows most where steps are short. Prefill runs host-planned and is unchanged.


## CI

The kernel test checks the decide kernel's runner inputs against the reference, and treats ids outside the experts as padding. `test_paged_experts.py` already runs captured paged decode end to end on GPTQ, FP8 and gpt-oss MXFP4.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing change.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -34,23 +34,39 @@ def _jit_module() -> Module:
 
 def paged_experts_decide(
     topk: torch.Tensor,
+    topk_weights: torch.Tensor,
     step: torch.Tensor,
     slot_expert: torch.Tensor,
     expert_slot: torch.Tensor,
     slot_lastuse: torch.Tensor,
     src: torch.Tensor,
     dst: torch.Tensor,
     count: torch.Tensor,
+    run_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    run_w: torch.Tensor,
 ) -> None:
     """Make every expert in ``topk`` (``[T]`` routed ids, negative = padding, ``T <= K``) resident.
 
     Keeps the resident ones, gives each missing one the least recently used slot the step does
     not need, and updates the residency state in place: ``step`` ``[1]``, ``slot_expert`` and
     ``slot_lastuse`` ``[K]``, ``expert_slot`` ``[E]``. Writes the page-in plan to ``src``/``dst``
-    ``[K]`` (expert -> slot) and its length to ``count`` ``[1]``.
+    ``[K]`` (expert -> slot) and its length to ``count`` ``[1]``, and the runner's inputs:
+    ``run_ids`` ``[T]`` int32, the slot holding each entry's expert, and ``run_w`` ``[T]``
+    float32, its weight from ``topk_weights`` ``[T]`` float32; padding entries (id outside
+    ``[0, E)``) get slot 0 and weight 0.
     """
     _jit_module().paged_experts_decide(
-        topk, step, slot_expert, expert_slot, slot_lastuse, src, dst, count
+        topk,
+        topk_weights,
+        step,
+        slot_expert,
+        expert_slot,
+        slot_lastuse,
+        src,
+        dst,
+        count,
+        run_ids,
+        run_w,
     )

@@ -113,21 +113,33 @@ def run(self, layer, dispatch_output):
         from sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher import StandardCombineInput
 
         r = self.residency
-        topk_ids = dispatch_output.topk_output.topk_ids
+        topk_output = dispatch_output.topk_output
+        topk_ids, topk_weights = topk_output.topk_ids, topk_output.topk_weights
+        run_ids = torch.empty(topk_ids.shape, dtype=torch.int32, device=topk_ids.device)
+        run_w = torch.empty(topk_ids.shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=topk_ids.device)
         paged_experts_decide(
             topk_ids.flatten().to(torch.int32),
+            topk_weights.flatten().to(torch.float32),
             r.step,
             r.slot_expert,
             r.expert_slot,
             r.slot_lastuse,
             r.src,
             r.dst,
             r.count,
+            run_ids.view(-1),
+            run_w.view(-1),
         )
         self.store.gather(src=r.src, dst=r.dst, count=r.count)
-        # Every routed expert is now resident; padding (-1) stays masked.
-        slots = r.expert_slot[topk_ids.clamp(min=0)].masked_fill(topk_ids < 0, -1)
-        partial = run_on_slots(self.base_method, layer, dispatch_output, slots)
+        # Every routed expert is now resident; padding got slot 0 and weight 0.
+        wave_output = dispatch_output._replace(
+            topk_output=topk_output._replace(
+                topk_ids=run_ids, topk_weights=run_w.to(topk_weights.dtype)
+            )
+        )
+        partial = self.base_method.apply(
+            layer=layer, dispatch_output=wave_output
+        ).hidden_states
         return StandardCombineInput(
             hidden_states=self.contract.finish(
                 merged=partial,

@@ -29,17 +29,25 @@ def __init__(self):
         self.dst = torch.zeros(K, **i32)
         self.count = torch.zeros(1, **i32)
 
-    def decide(self, topk):
+    def decide(self, topk, weights=None):
+        """Run the decide kernel; return the runner inputs it wrote (slots, weights)."""
+        if weights is None:
+            weights = torch.ones(topk.shape, device="cuda")
+        run_ids, run_w = torch.empty_like(topk), torch.empty_like(weights)
         paged_experts_decide(
             topk,
+            weights,
             self.step,
             self.slot_expert,
             self.expert_slot,
             self.slot_lastuse,
             self.src,
             self.dst,
             self.count,
+            run_ids,
+            run_w,
         )
+        return run_ids, run_w
 
 
 class _Reference:
@@ -87,13 +95,29 @@ def assert_state(self, state, ref, plan):
         self.assertEqual(state.expert_slot.tolist(), expert_slot)
 
     def test_decide_matches_reference(self):
+        """The LRU decision and plan, and the runner inputs: each entry's slot and weight,
+        slot 0 and weight 0 for padding."""
         generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
         state, ref = _State(), _Reference()
         for _ in range(200):
             topk = _random_topk(generator, int(torch.randint(1, K + 1, (1,))))
+            weights = torch.rand(topk.shape, generator=generator)
             plan = ref.decide(topk.tolist())
-            state.decide(topk.cuda())
+            run_ids, run_w = state.decide(topk.cuda(), weights.cuda())
             self.assert_state(state, ref, plan)
+            routed = topk >= 0
+            slots = [ref.slot_expert.index(e) if e >= 0 else 0 for e in topk.tolist()]
+            self.assertEqual(run_ids.tolist(), slots)
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(run_w.cpu(), weights.masked_fill(~routed, 0)))
+
+    def test_decide_pads_ids_outside_the_experts(self):
+        topk = torch.tensor([3, E, -1, 3, E + 5], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        weights = torch.arange(1, 6, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+        state = _State()
+        run_ids, run_w = state.decide(topk, weights)
+        self.assertEqual(run_ids.tolist(), [3, 0, 0, 3, 0])
+        self.assertEqual(run_w.tolist(), [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0, 0.0])
+        self.assertEqual(state.count.item(), 0)
 
     def test_decide_rejects_more_entries_than_slots(self):
         with self.assertRaises(Exception):
